definitions.explanation: Words without substance or truth; something said that has no basis in reality. Has a somewhat literary or classical tone.

examples.japanese: あれは{空言|そらごと}にすぎない。
examples.english: That is nothing but empty words.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}の{約束|やくそく}は{空言|そらごと}だった。
いくら{美|うつく}しい{言葉|ことば}を{並|なら}べても、{行動|こうどう}が{伴|ともな}わなければ{空言|そらごと}に{終|お}わる。
examples.english: No matter how many fine words you line up, without action they end up as empty talk.

notes:
A compound of {空|そら} (empty, sky — here meaning 'empty' or 'hollow') + {言|ごと} (words, saying). A somewhat literary or elevated word for a lie or empty talk.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {空言|そらごと}を{言|い}う: to tell lies, to speak empty words
- {空言|そらごと}にすぎない: to be nothing but empty words
- {空言|そらごと}に{終|お}わる: to end up as mere words

REGISTER:
This word has a literary, somewhat classical feel. In everyday conversation, {嘘|うそ} (lie) or {口先|くちさき}だけ (lip service) are more common. {空言|そらごと} tends to appear in written language, formal speech, or proverbs.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {嘘|うそ}: lie — the most common everyday word for an untruth
- {虚言|きょげん}: falsehood, fabrication — a more formal synonym
- {戯言|たわごと}: nonsense, idle talk — emphasizes absurdity rather than deception
